ideas.title: Ride it down: Lumi on the cart over the crest, one brake lever with three throws
ideas.critique: This merges round 2's two braking pitches into one played ride, and that fixes what each lacked on its own: the current reversing by itself against the pots' EMF and a short-circuit strap that can slip the belt are now two options that trade off against each other, on ground nobody laid by hand. The physics decides both scores, so it is a judgement you can get better at, the first one on the island. The weak spots are Lumi 'seated with its hand on the lever', which is easy to fake as a pose glued to the deck, and the stake, which becomes a fixed target to memorise if the crest is always the same one.

ideas.title: The cart takes the dune: Lumi rides, and the charge decides where it stops
ideas.critique: This is the big goal's dune run itself. The pots' state carries over from day to day, so a drained climb shows up the next day, which is the come-back-every-day loop done for real. Planning a road for least charge spent is a genuine optimisation game. It is also the vaguest pitch: 'it brakes itself' over the crest takes the player's hand off the one moment that is most fun to judge, and if laying a plank means clicking to snap it in place, the building half is a road editor sitting on top of a good Sim.
